title: Is there any other even number that is prime?
description: Two is a prime and also even. The board lists the factors of the even numbers bigger than two and counts them, and each list holds at least three factors.
teaching_notes: One idea: every even number bigger than two has the factors one, two and itself, so it has more than two factors. Watch for students who think a small even number such as four is prime.

video_script.why: The child decides whether an even number can be prime by counting its factors, the same way as the example in the book that sorts numbers into primes and composites.
video_script.substitution: List the factors of even numbers bigger than two and count them.
video_script.anchor: A row of even numbers on the board, with their factors listed under them
video_script.payoff_line: No other even number is prime, because two divides every even number bigger than two.

final_answer.spoken: no, two is the only even prime

maths_rules: a prime has exactly two factors, 1 and itself
factors of 4: 1, 2, 4 (3 factors); of 6: 1, 2, 3, 6 (4 factors); of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8 (4 factors)
every even number n bigger than 2 has the factors 1, 2 and n, which are 3 different factors
check with 10: 10 = 2 × 5, factors 1, 2, 5, 10 (4 factors), so 10 is not prime
video_script.design: Three even numbers are split by two and their factors listed; the count of factors is circled in the warning colour when it is more than two.
